location: runtime/loop/config-drift.mjs:214-241 (detectBrainDrift's resolveExpectedValue-on-both-sides fix), runtime/loop/config.mjs:104-113 (loadConfig's dotenv precedence layer), runtime/loop/index.mjs:81-82 (dotenvText read + merged into config BEFORE process.env is the only source `ps` can see)
description:
This is the exact false-negative class the reviewing lead asked me to attack hardest, and it is real. The iteration-2 'live-run correctness fix' makes an OBSERVED env object that simply omits a key resolve to `codeDefault` ('proxy') the same way an unobserved-key DECLARED config does (config-drift.mjs:214-222, tested at config-drift.test.mjs:145-148 and config-drift-detector.test.mjs:126-142 — 'neither side explicitly sets ANICCA_BRAIN ... both inherit the identical codeDefault -> PASS'). This fix's entire correctness depends on an unstated assumption: that when `ps -Awwe -E` shows no `ANICCA_BRAIN=` token for a process, that process's TRUE effective `config.ANICCA_BRAIN` is genuinely the hardcoded 'proxy' default. That assumption is FALSE in this very codebase: `runtime/loop/config.mjs:104-113`'s `loadConfig(processEnv, dotenvText)` resolves `ANICCA_BRAIN` with precedence `processEnv[key] ?? dotenvValues[key] ?? DEFAULTS[key]` -- and `dotenvValues` comes from `$ANICCA_HOME/.env`, read and parsed entirely inside the Node process (index.mjs:81-82: `const dotenvText = await readDotenvFile(ANICCA_HOME); const config = loadConfig(process.env, dotenvText);`) WITHOUT ever being written back into `process.env`. A value set only via `$ANICCA_HOME/.env` is therefore invisible to `ps -Awwe -E` (which can only show the OS-level process environment, not this Node app's in-memory merged config object) while still being the process's real, governing `ANICCA_BRAIN` value.
Concretely: if an instance's plist never declares `ANICCA_BRAIN` (declaredConfig={} -> falls back to codeDefault 'proxy', the intended REQ-001 edge-case behavior) AND that instance's `$ANICCA_HOME/.env` sets `ANICCA_BRAIN=claude-p` (a real, supported override mechanism this same config.mjs implements), the running process's TRUE effective brain is `claude-p` -- but `ps` shows no `ANICCA_BRAIN=` token at all, so the 'fixed' detector computes `actual = codeDefault = 'proxy'` and reports ZERO drift, exactly the 'declared+observed both silent -> assume codeDefault -> PASS' pattern the lead asked me to check for swallowing real drift. This is precisely the same category of bug (Bug 1: declared config diverges from the value that actually governs runtime behavior) the entire feature exists to catch, recurring through a DIFFERENT, already-supported channel (.env) that the detector's model of 'actual' (ps env tokens only) cannot see -- the spec's own REQ-001 EARS text scopes 'actual' narrowly to 'ps -Awwe 実行時コマンドライン中の ANICCA_BRAIN= 値' without ever addressing this channel, and no REQ/edge-case/test anywhere considers `$ANICCA_HOME/.env` as a source of the effective runtime value the detector is supposed to be verifying against. (No `.env` file in the current fleet happens to set ANICCA_BRAIN today -- grepped `~/.anicca-founder/.env` and `~/.anicca/**` for the string, zero matches -- so this is not an active false negative in TODAY's fleet, but it is a real, reachable, currently-untested gap in the detector's own model of 'what actually governs this process's brain', not a hypothetical.)
requiredFix: Either (a) extend REQ-001's declared/actual definitions and the detector's `readPlistEnv`/observed-side resolution to also account for `$ANICCA_HOME/.env`'s ANICCA_BRAIN override (so the detector's model of 'actual' matches loadConfig's real precedence, not just the OS-level env), or (b) explicitly scope the spec to state that `.env`-sourced overrides are out of scope for this feature with a documented rationale, so a future reader does not mistake the current narrow ps-only definition for completeness. Add a test that exercises this specific gap (a fixture where ps shows no ANICCA_BRAIN token but the instance's real config would resolve it via .env) so the choice is enforced rather than implicit.
